pr_title: Write JSON to stdErr / stdOut if not using console.
pr_body:
Update `Terminal` to optionally emit JSON for both stdErr and stdOut in `ServerCli` if enabled through the environment variables `ELASTIC_CONTAINER` and `ES_LOG_STYLE`. This is typically the case for docker containers.

An additional pump thread for stdout makes sure any lines emitted there are converted to Json if necessary.

(Closes #96996)
pr_comments:
> One thing I think still missing is adjusting ServerProcess so that stdout of the process is captured/pumped, so that we can convert to json (only stderr is captured now).

I've been wondering about this @rjernst and I'm personally not convinced we should be doing that. My thoughts on this are:

- We should prevent anyone from directly writing to stdout in elasticsearch (and we try that by declaring those APIs forbidden). But if circumvented and done anyways, I would consider that a bug that requires fixing. `Bootstrap` currently exposes a stdOut `PrintWriter`, but according to your comment this should be removed. (Do you want me to do that?)

- Also, other than `stderr`, `stdout` is fairly high throughput due to logging, meaning significantly more work to pump things through.

- Last, we're still somehow assumption driven when deciding to use a JSON terminal. We can't be certain about the actual log4j2 configuration, e.g. someone might have overwritten log4j2.properties in a customized container to use a different layout (though, likely not something we'd like to support intentionally). But admitted, the same way log4j2 could be configured to log on stderr.

> We should prevent anyone from directly writing to stdout in elasticsearch

We do prevent that already. The reason for capturing stdout/stderr and converting to json is for messages output by the JDK which may have handles to the original output stream before we replaced it without log4j based streams (or more likely, output before ES actually started executing). I'm not sure we can be sure the JDK only ever emits messages to stderr only.

> stdout is fairly high throughput due to logging

I think the throughput should be ok. Here is my thinking: we only check the first character, and messages we actually need to convert to json are rare (since they come from the jdk), so the work should be minimal. Additionally, ES logs are generally not high throughput to begin with because we don't do request logging.

> We can't be certain about the actual log4j2 configuration

This is a fair concern. I wonder if we could document the constraints/expectations. Custom log4j configuration is a very advanced feature, and we make changes all the time to our log4j config, which would have to be replicated by anyone customizing the config.

> I'm not sure we can be sure the JDK only ever emits messages to stderr only.

Ok, fair point. I've added the pump for Stdout. Though, a couple of observations on the code. See the other comments

> I wonder if we could document the constraints/expectations. Custom log4j configuration is a very advanced feature, and we make changes all the time to our log4j config, which would have to be replicated by anyone customizing the config.

Looking at the [ES docker docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.12/docker.html), any reference of `ES_LOG_STYLE` was apparently intentionally removed for more recent versions and no mention of logging formats there. The [logging docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.12/logging.html), on the other hand, don't mention any specifics for Docker containers.
what would happen if we run docker, but configure logging to files in a side container? Like in ESS, and likely in serverless soon?

> what would happen if we run docker, but configure logging to files in a side container? Like in ESS, and likely in serverless soon?

This is based on `ES_LOG_STYLE`. If disabling the default JSON console logs by setting `ES_LOG_STYLE=file`, JSON output is also disabled. The trouble is really that we try to match the log layout in cases where logs are send to stderr (or stdout) without being able to really understand the log4j2 configuration. In a way this will always be speculative, but with that said it should be a very conservative guess with as little as possible false positives to not make things worse.

> what would happen if we run docker, but configure logging to files in a side container? Like in ESS, and likely in serverless soon?

@rjernst what are your thoughts regarding O11Y-516 / the point @pgomulka brought up above?
We've decided on another approach, I'll follow up with a new PR

issue_context.title: `Elasticsearch exited unexpectedly` is not JSON
issue_context.body: When running in certain environments we expect that the output to `stderr` and `stdout` comprises JSON logs, with timestamps and so on. But if Elasticsearch exits then we log the bare string `ERROR: Elasticsearch exited unexpectedly`. Can we make this JSON? Can we include a timestamp? It'd be awfully useful to know when exactly the exit occurred.
comments:
> Can we make this JSON?

The output format for stdout / stderr is defined based on the log4j2 layout used for the console appender (log4j2.properties), this can obviously vary between environments. Cli tools are currently not using log4j2, instead we're directly writing to stout / stderr (based on a `Terminal` implementation). No matter how we change the output format in cli tools, it'll always be inconsistent in some environments unless based on the same configuration.

If we consider this to be really important, we could think about a terminal that writes to stdout / stderr through log4j.
Though, cli tools / the launcher were designed with minimal dependencies in mind. That would obviously change then.

> Can we include a timestamp?

Just including a timestamp is certainly trivial and easy to do independent of the previous point.

> If we consider this to be really important, we could think about a terminal that writes to stdout / stderr through log4j.
> Though, cli tools / the launcher were designed with minimal dependencies in mind. That would obviously change then.

We should consider if this is possible. Doing something ad-hoc is going to mean trying to detect if JSON output for stdout/stderr is enabled. Since this is currently controlled by log4j properties, there's no way the CLI tools will know this without a) parsing those properties or b) introducing some other signal (system prop, environment variable, etc). If we go with (a) we might as well just use log4j in the CLI tools and (b) will undoubtedly get out of sync given all the different packaging types we have and logging config overrides.

I think it's a little more complicated than just using log4j within the CLI tools. It's not just about the messages the CLI outputs directly. The CLI has to capture and pass through stderr currently to look for special signals from the ES process (eg ready signal). The JDK can sometimes output things to stderr (maybe stdout too?) that are plain text. The CLI already sees that plain text, but just passes it through unaware. But other output from the process may already be in json, so we can't just jsonify everything output to stderr/stdout.

As far as outputting json from the cli, while we do already configure logging, I'm not sure we want to complicate Terminal with log4j. Terminal has it's own concepts for log levels, which are not the same as general logging. We also don't need full featured json, we have very limited needs here.

For detecting when to output in JSON, we already know when we are in the Docker packaging, which is when we output logs to JSON, so we can use the same thing in selecting which Terminal output type to use in CliToolLauncher.

> For detecting when to output in JSON, we already know when we are in the Docker packaging, which is when we output logs to JSON, so we can use the same thing in selecting which Terminal output type to use in CliToolLauncher.

Right now this is the case and 1:1 but that's not necessarily guaranteed to always be so. Probably "good enough" if going full log4j is impractical though.

@rjernst I've pushed a draft PR (see above), let me know if the general approach makes sense to you. 
The new output obviously breaks a lot of assumptions in the packaging tests. If you're good to proceed that way I'll tackle those next.

could we use System.Logger in the CLI tools? In CLI it would default to console logger (and perhaps create a json style console System.Logger) 
but if log4j2 configuration is present it woudl return log4j2 impl?
this would only fix the dependency problem. Not sure how to work around the problem with log4j configuration being loaded later..

review_comments: Can you add a test with printing a stack trace from an exception? I suspect we will get multiple json objects, one per line of the stack trace. If so, we should re-plumb where exceptions are handled for the cli to work a little different. Similar question with the help message output, or anywhere we grab the PrintWriter directly.

Yes, usage of `Exception#printStackTrace` would result in stracktraces being scattered across multiple json objects. Looking at the code, I also noticed everything but UserException and OptionException bubble through uncaught and wouldn't be logged as JSON at all. I'll follow up on that.
Help messages should be alright, but I'll verify.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104055/commits/c191edce596b662e003c2652e89c2c6c3392c78e adds support to write a stacktrace into a single JSON object. Though, that also requires to catch all exceptions before exciting `main`.
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104055/commits/d1e75e0f88168de5e7bc41e0ed5cd31be1cc7545 verifies the behavior with respect to the option parser / printing help.

I think there are some other fields we should fill in. eg `log.level`, `log.logger`. Perhaps others, are any other fields required by ECS (eg `ecs.version)? Will we be able to find these messages associated with a node if we don't output `elasticsearch.node.name` and `elasticsearch.cluster.name`? cc @pgomulka

we should be able to still find those logs as filebeat will add additional fields like `docker.container.name` or `ece.cluster` `ece.instance`. in ESS cloud is still parsing .log files instead of json files, so it proves it is doable :) , but raises a question if we should stream the stdout/err to both plaintext log and json (if this change applies to all distributions)

`elasticsearch.node.name`  is dynamically set because it can be generated if no `node.name` is provided. So not sure you can easily use it here without logging dependencies.

`elasticsearch.cluster.name` is based on a static setting based on `cluster.name` setting. Might be worth setting that field.


node.id, cluster.uuid are both dynamically generated and stored in thread context - again it would be hard to access them here.

I agree we should set log.level and log.logger.
but also `event.dataset` = `elasticsearch.server` (or elasticserach.stdout?)

service.name = ES_ECS
perhaps ecs.version = 1.12.0

> but raises a question if we should stream the stdout/err to both plaintext log and json

Note that this is the CLI process. I don't think we should try writing to log files. We are only trying to ensure that when ES is emitting json to stdout/stderr, the CLI also emits json. This can happen in two ways: (1) if the cli logs something and (2) if the ES process emits non-json directly from the jdk (this would normally only happen early in startup, before ES has replaced the stdout/stderr streams).

>  ESS cloud is still parsing .log files instead of json files

Is that true? Sounds like they discard stderr / stdout of the launcher then?

> I think there are some other fields we should fill in. eg log.level, log.logger. Perhaps others, are any other fields required by ECS 

That's part of the reason why I initially considered depending on ecs-logging-core. As @pgomulka pointed out some field require additionally logic defined in the logging dependencies.

- `logger`: that one is simple to add ✔️ 
- `level`: are we good with a static level per PrintWriter (INFO for stdout, ERROR for stderr)? PrintWriter isn't aware of the Terminal verbosity level, but required (for instance, the JSON print writer is passed to the options parser). So that would require some ThreadLocal hack then. 

I'll give this a closer look tomorrow 👍

I've added a couple of fields in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104055/commits/47f4d7ddd21676397104b38799aed1a85bb8df48:
- `log.level`: `ERROR` for stderr, `INFO` for `stdout`. I decided against using the verbosity concept. First, that concept is unknown if the `PrintWriter` is used outside of `Terminal`. Second, multiple line parts might be collapsed into a single JSON message with possibly different verbosity levels.
- `log.logger`: `stderr` for stderr, `stdout` for `stdout`.
- `service.name`: `ES_ECS`
- `event.dataset`: `elasticsearch.server`

The `cluster.name` setting isn't available at this point, and there's quite a number of different ways how settings can be set and what's prioritised in what order. IMHO I'd rather not set it than risking a divergence here.

Looks like the current `ecs-logging-core` is at (ecs) version `1.2.0`. `1.12.0` seems far ahead if that's the most recent version. Is that something we really want to maintain manually here?
These look good to start with, we can consider more in followups. As for ecs version, I'm not sure how much it matters, maybe @pgomulka has more thoughts there.
